header.title: Call Debrief — Pat Doe
header.subtitle: GM, Riverbend Auto Group · Called Fri Jun 12 · Outcome: agreed to a 30-day test, terms TBD

captureQuestions.text: When you said his salespeople were "like a soccer coach with no roster," what did Pat's face do?
captureQuestions.why: The recording catches your words but not his reaction — and his reaction is the whole point.
captureQuestions.anchorQuote: ...it's like a soccer coach showing up with no roster, right?

captureQuestions.text: You answered the price question a third time, and that's where it got long. What set that off?
captureQuestions.why: You told me over-explaining past the yes is the habit you want to catch. This is where it started.
captureQuestions.anchorQuote: ...so on price, again, the way it works is...

planVsReality.planned: Book a 30-day dealer test on one rooftop. Hold the frame — not another lead vendor — and get a small, measurable yes.
planVsReality.happened: He's interested and said yes in principle to a test, but didn't lock a rooftop or a start date. He kept circling back to price and to his existing lead spend.

conflicts.operatorSaid: Your note says "Pat's in, just need to send terms."
conflicts.transcriptSaid: On the call he said "let me run it by my GM partner first" and never gave a start date.
conflicts.resolve: Treat this as a soft yes, not a closed test. Before you log it as won, confirm the partner conversation happened. Send terms AND ask for a specific start date in the same email.

wentWell.point: You opened on his close rate, not your product.
wentWell.why: Carnegie: he gave you the number (18% on bought leads) because the first question was about his world. That number became the whole hook.

wentWell.point: You held the frame when he called you 'another vendor.'
wentWell.why: Klaff: you didn't get defensive or discount — you re-anchored on 'your own traffic, not shared leads.' That's the line that kept you out of supplicant mode.

toImprove.point: You let the close stay vague — no rooftop, no date.
toImprove.fix: Freese: ask for the small, specific yes. 'Which rooftop, and can we start Monday the 22nd?' A test with no date isn't a test, it's a maybe.

toImprove.point: You answered the price question three times.
toImprove.fix: Klaff: answering it twice was fine; the third time you started justifying. Park it once: 'Price is easy and I'll put it in writing — the real question is whether seeing your own in-market shoppers is worth a 30-day look.'

prospectRead: Pat believes the problem is real — he knows he's wasting spend on shared leads. He's not blocked on belief, he's blocked on risk and on not being the only decision-maker. The partner mention is real, not a brush-off. Lower his risk (short, cancel-anytime, one rooftop) and arm him to sell it internally and he moves.
nextCallGoal: Lock a specific rooftop and a start date for the 30-day test — and confirm the GM partner is a yes, not a veto.

autoDone: Logged the call outcome on Pat's Close lead.

needsYou.action: Send the terms + start-date email to Pat
needsYou.why: External send — leaves your inbox, so it's your call to send.

needsYou.action: Decide whether to offer a second rooftop as a sweetener
needsYou.why: Pricing/packaging judgment — your decision, not the system's.

needsInfo.for: Confirmation his GM partner is on board + a start date

followups.subject: Your 30-day test — terms + a start date
followups.draft:
Pat — great talking today, and thanks for the straight answer on your close rate.

Here's the simple version of the 30-day test: one rooftop, we show you the in-market shoppers already on your own site, no long-term commitment, cancel anytime. I'll put the price in writing so there's no mystery.

Two quick things so we can start clean: which rooftop do you want to run it on, and can we kick off Monday the 22nd? Happy to hop on a 10-minute call with your GM partner if it helps him get comfortable.

nextGuideSeed: Next call goal: lock the rooftop + start date and clear the GM-partner question. He's a soft yes blocked on risk and on not being sole decision-maker. Lead with risk-reduction (short, cancel-anytime, one rooftop) and arm him to sell it internally. Park price after answering once.
crmLog: Outcome: Soft yes to a 30-day test, no rooftop/date locked. Held the frame well (own-traffic vs shared leads), close left vague. Blocker: GM partner not yet bought in + risk. Next: send terms + ask for rooftop & start date (Mon 6/22), offer 10-min call with partner. Watch: don't log as won until partner confirmed.
